newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.5 pct, seen resuming uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.5 pct, seen resuming uptrend.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 2.51 percent in selective buying led by shares of largely state-owned firms on Thursday, resuming a medium-term uptrend after drifting sideways for two weeks, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 gained 2,041.29 points, or 2.51 percent to close at 83,505.37, compared to an all-time high of 83,772.33 on October 23.
Trade volume was 17.39 trillion lira, down from 19.27 trillion on Wednesday.
Brokers said selective buys flared in the second session after the index remained in a tight range in thin morning trade.

"Heavy buying began in shares of state companies like Tupras, Petrol Ofisi, Turkish Airlines and spilled over to other stocks. Activity in the state shares was based on privatisation expectations," said Hakan Demirbulak from Tatbank.
"The index seems to have turned upward from 81,500 support following a pull back," he added.
The market index had surged 29.3 percent, breaking ten record closes from September 13 to October 23 in the medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level.
It went into range-trading after failing to pierce stiff resistance at 85,000 barrier last Thursday.

Actives were led by utility Aktas Elektrik, down 2,000 lira at 98,000, Turkish Airlines, up 2,250 lira at 24,250, largely state owned petroleum refiner Tupras, up 2,250 lira at 21,250 and petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi, up 1,500 lira at 30,000.
"The market found firm support at around 81,000 and will now try the upside after the down correction," said Lokman Esref from Alan securities.

Of the 227 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 145 to 46 and 36 ended steady. The 85-share industrial index rose 1.71 percent to 87,829.95 and the 15-share financial index surged 4.29 percent to 81,624.11.
